tldr: This paper presents a rotation-optimal algorithm for noncommutative prefix scans in bit-reversed homomorphic encryption layouts, reducing the number of cyclic rotations required.
motivation: Packed homomorphic encryption enables parallel slotwise operations, but nonlocal communication via cyclic rotations is costly. The paper aims to minimize the number of rotations for ordered prefix computation on elements stored in bit-reversed order.
method: The authors introduce a replicated-aggregate invariant where each slot of an aligned logical block stores the same complete block aggregate, allowing one global rotation per level to supply valid sibling aggregates. They prove exact bounds on the number of rotations and depth.
result: The algorithm achieves O(log n) rotations and depth, with exact bounds proven. Implementation in CKKS shows significant reductions in rotations, evaluation-key storage, peak heap usage, and latency compared to a direct bit-reversed baseline.
conclusion: The proposed replicated scan is rotation-optimal for noncommutative prefix scans in bit-reversed homomorphic layouts, improving efficiency in homomorphic encryption applications.

title: Second-Order Quantifier Elimination And Uniform Interpolation For Bath Path Logic And The Ordered Fragment
authors: Hongkai Yin Renate A. Schmidt
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider and extend results on basic path logic and the ordered fragment of first-order logic, both of which originate from the functional translation of modal logic. Basic path logic is a subclass of the clausal class for the [MATH]-fragment and has the remarkable property that binary resolution decides it. This decidability result and the consequence finding completeness of binary resolution allows us to observe that binary resolution also decides uniform interpolation and computes uniform interpolants for basic path logic. By introducing constant Skolemisation, we show that sentences of the ordered fragment can be transformed into basic path logic, and this transformation preserves logical consequences in the ordered fragment. We characterise the search space of the SCAN algorithm on the clausal form of the ordered fragment by a variation of basic path logic and prove that SCAN terminates on this class, and therefore it decides second-order quantifier elimination for this class. It remains unclear whether uniform interpolants in the ordered fragment can be extracted from the output of SCAN.
tldr: This paper extends results on basic path logic and the ordered fragment of first-order logic, focusing on second-order quantifier elimination and uniform interpolation.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the search space of the SCAN algorithm for second-order quantifier elimination and to determine whether uniform interpolants can be extracted from its output.
method: The paper introduces constant Skolemisation to transform sentences of the ordered fragment into basic path logic, and uses binary resolution to decide uniform interpolation for basic path logic.
result: Binary resolution decides uniform interpolation for basic path logic, and SCAN terminates on the clausal form of the ordered fragment, thus deciding second-order quantifier elimination for this class.
conclusion: It remains unclear whether uniform interpolants in the ordered fragment can be extracted from the output of SCAN.

title: ThreatVisionAI: A Hybrid CNN-ViT Framework For Image-Based Malware Classification
authors: Prashanth Busireddygari Allyson Taylor
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional malware detection methods struggle to generalize to obfuscated or previously unseen threats. This paper introduces ThreatVisionAI, a hybrid malware family classification framework that integrates a raw-image CNN, a wavelet-based CNN, and a Vision Transformer (ViT) to capture complementary spatial, frequency-domain, and global relational features in malware images. The wavelet-based CNN captures multi-scale frequency information that helps distinguish closely related families, while the ViT branch models long-range dependencies across the image. Evaluated on the Malimg dataset, ThreatVisionAI achieves 98.01% accuracy and a weighted F1 score of 0.9742, with wavelet-domain features providing measurable gains on minority and visually similar families. These results confirm that frequency-aware and transformer-based representations improve image-based malware family classification.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid CNN-ViT framework for malware image classification, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Traditional malware detection methods struggle with obfuscated threats, motivating a hybrid deep learning approach.
method: The framework combines a raw-image CNN, a wavelet-based CNN, and a Vision Transformer to capture spatial, frequency, and global features from malware images.
result: The model achieves 98.01% accuracy and a weighted F1 score of 0.9742 on the Malimg dataset, with wavelet features improving minority class performance.
conclusion: Frequency-aware and transformer-based representations enhance image-based malware classification.

title: A Failure-Mode Benchmark For Polymorphic Sybil Poisoning In Rag
authors: Juntae Kim Donghyun Lee (dongguk University)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We release a benchmark and failure-mode-aware evaluation framework for grounded QA under coordinated retrieval poisoning. The framework partitions reader outputs into four mutually exclusive categories (, , , ), with instance-level paired clean-to-poison transition matrices and a Forced Exposure protocol isolating reader-side conflict resolution from retrieval variance. We introduce , a coordinated attack class in which [MATH] lexically diverse passages jointly support an attacker-chosen target while evading lexical near-duplicate filters that fully detect monomorphic baselines (capturing the residual 14.2\% with E5 cosine raises false-positive rate 9[MATH] on legitimate same-topic pairs). A monomorphic-polymorphic ablation under Forced Exposure isolates the diversity dimension and reveals a [MATH]18.8pp hijack amplification (95\% paired bootstrap CI [MATH], [MATH]): monomorphic copies register only 4.0\% as hijack while polymorphic surface diversity recovers 22.8\% -- a 5.7[MATH] amplification of the ASR-visible attack channel. ASR alone treats every non-target output identically; under attack, abstention and drift together hold 47-66\% of output mass, unmonitored by ASR+ACC, and two readers at nearly identical ASR (within 0.2pp) differ by 16.5pp on abstention and 17.2pp on drift -- failure profiles invisible to ASR. We release the frozen benchmark (3{,}145 questions, 2{,}982 retained sybil groups; [MATH] chosen to dominate top-10 retrieval slots, \S), the official four-way evaluator, paired-transition utilities, and the Forced Exposure harness across five readers (7B-120B), two retrievers, and two cross-validation datasets (TriviaQA, 2Wiki), under CC~BY-SA~4.0 (data) and MIT (software); release information in \S.
tldr: This paper presents a benchmark and evaluation framework for grounded question answering under coordinated retrieval poisoning, focusing on polymorphic sybil attacks.
motivation: Current retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are vulnerable to adversarial poisoning of the retrieval corpus, but existing evaluations overlook the diversity of attack strategies and failure modes beyond simple answer accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a benchmark with 3,145 questions and 2,982 sybil groups, a four-way output categorization (correct, hijack, abstain, drift), and a Forced Exposure protocol to isolate reader-side conflict resolution from retrieval variance. They compare monomorphic and polymorphic sybil attacks.
result: Polymorphic sybil attacks achieve 22.8% hijack rate vs. 4.0% for monomorphic, a 5.7× amplification, and two readers with nearly identical answer success rates differ by 16.5pp in abstention and 17.2pp in drift, revealing failure modes invisible to standard metrics.
conclusion: The benchmark and evaluation framework expose critical failure modes in RAG systems under coordinated poisoning, highlighting the need for more nuanced security evaluations beyond answer accuracy.

title: A Modern View On MCSat
authors: Thomas Hader, Theo Jauschneg, Daniela Kaufmann, Laura Kovacs
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Constructing Satisfiability (MCSat) approach has shown strong performance in solving complex SMT problems, in particular in algebraic SMT theories such as non-linear integer and real arithmetic. In this paper we revisit the theory-independent MCSat framework as a proof system to provide a modern perspective that refines the original formulation of MCSat. By closely formalizing the implementation of MCSat within the Yices2 SMT solver, we incorporate design decisions that diverge from those in the seminal MCSat paper and thereby capture the current state-of-the-art in MCSat-based SMT reasoning. We present a general, theory-agnostic rule scheme for MCSat and instantiate it for several theories, including propositional logic, non-linear real arithmetic, and uninterpreted functions. We provide several detailed examples to illustrate the applicability of the presented calculus.
tldr: This paper presents a modern formalization of the MCSat proof system for SMT solving, focusing on theory-independent reasoning and implementation in Yices2.
motivation: To provide a refined, up-to-date perspective on the MCSat framework that captures current state-of-the-art SMT reasoning, diverging from the original formulation.
method: The authors formalize a general, theory-agnostic rule scheme for MCSat and instantiate it for propositional logic, non-linear real arithmetic, and uninterpreted functions, closely following the Yices2 implementation.
result: A modernized MCSat calculus with detailed examples demonstrating its applicability across multiple theories.
conclusion: The refined MCSat framework offers a more accurate representation of current SMT solving techniques and can serve as a basis for further theoretical and practical developments.

title: DualView: Preventing Indirect Prompt Injection In Personal Ai Agents
authors: Juhee Kim, Woohyuk Choi, Taehyun Kang, Youngmin Kim, Byoungyoung Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal AI agents that run on the user's local machine, such as OpenClaw, automate daily tasks including web search, email, and file management. Their access to computer resources, including the network, file system, and shell, exposes them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks. Prior Dual LLM defenses block IPI by replacing untrusted data with symbols that the agent can reference but not read. However, they track untrusted data only inside the agent's context, so when the agent saves and later rereads untrusted data, that data, possibly an attacker's prompt, can return as trusted data rather than as a symbol, which we call stored IPI. Operating on the user's real environment, which humans and programs share, is what makes agents like OpenClaw practical, and is exactly why a defense that ignores it is incomplete. Preserving symbols in such an environment is hard, because humans and programs need original data. We present DualView, which extends untrusted data tracking from the agent's context to the user's environment, including the file system, shell, network, and other agents, by giving each channel two views. In AgentView, the agent sees untrusted data as symbols even after writing it out and reading it back, blocking stored IPI, while HumanView preserves original data for humans and tools. DualView routes each tool call to the right view and synchronizes data across the two views. DualView deploys as an OpenClaw plugin using only tool hooks, without changing the agent's tool-call logic or tool implementations. Since DualView isolates untrusted data by design, its protection is not limited to known attack templates. In our evaluation on an IPI benchmark and PinchBench, DualView blocked every IPI attack, including stored IPI, while keeping utility close to the unprotected baseline.
tldr: The paper presents DualView, a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in personal AI agents by extending untrusted data tracking to the user's environment.
motivation: Personal AI agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, and existing defenses fail to handle stored IPI when untrusted data is saved and later reread.
method: DualView gives each channel (file system, shell, network) two views: AgentView shows untrusted data as symbols, while HumanView preserves original data, routing tool calls appropriately.
result: DualView blocked all IPI attacks in evaluation, including stored IPI, while maintaining utility close to the unprotected baseline.
conclusion: DualView provides a robust defense against IPI by design, without requiring changes to agent logic or tool implementations.
